newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says no more tax, forex amnesties.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says no more tax, forex amnesties.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Tuesday that people with undeclared funds in or out of the country would not receive more amnesties after the present one expired in August.

"After the expiry of the six-month amnesty, tax enforcement will be further strengthened and strict sanctions will be imposed against tax evaders and those who violate foreign exchange regulations," a finance ministry statement said.
"It is anticipated that the amnesty would induce a substantial inflow of undisclosed funds that are alleged to be retained abroad.
"Such inflow of foreign exchange will improve our balance of payment position and make available more funds for productive investment in Sri Lanka," the statement added
The tax and foreign exchange amnesty began on February 15 and expires on August 15.
The statement said the amnesty was a chance for those who have evaded taxes or violated exchange control laws, to come clean.
Funds declared under the amnesty would have to be deposited in a special account in the state-owned National Savings Bank.
Funds being returned must be converted into local currency and deposited in the account within the stipulated six-month period.
Withdrawal from the deposits in the first two years would be allowed only for investments in agriculture, industry or infrastructure, the statement said.
